analysis_notes.notes: Torah LM2/52 contains zero bechina edges in the dataset. Both edges with reference=1052 are type 'cause' (cause-and-effect): (1) מעצם גדלתו ורוממותו, שהוא מרומם מאד מדעתנו → causes → אי אפשר שנבין ונשיג בשכלנו הנהגתו יתברך, (2) אי אפשר שנבין ונשיג בשכלנו הנהגתו יתברך → causes → שיהיו עליו יתברך קשיות. The source text (torah_52.txt) is among the briefest teachings in LM2 — two short paragraphs, a compressed oral saying. It contains no bechina language whatsoever: no use of 'בְּחִינַת', 'הוּא בְּחִינַת', 'נִקְרָא', or any parallel-nature identification. The entire teaching operates on a single logical-causal axis: God's infinite exaltedness above human understanding → impossibility of grasping His ways → necessary existence of unanswerable questions (kushiyot) about Him. The first paragraph extends this by analogy: tzaddikim resemble (מִתְדַּמִּים) their Creator, therefore questions about tzaddikim are likewise necessary. The word 'מִתְדַּמִּים' (they resemble) is not bechina language — it denotes a likeness-by-resemblance produced by closeness to God, not an identity of essential nature. No concepts in the source text are candidates for bechina-based package membership. Accordingly, no gap additions apply and no unassigned dataset nodes exist.
